ch-5.brief:
### Scenario
Your team runs an internal **LLM gateway**: every product team (a *tenant*) sends prompts to
it, and the gateway decides which model serves each request. Money is tracked in integer
*credits*. Over four levels you grow it from a budget checker into a router with fallback,
a response cache and spend metrics, the same shape as real gateways (LiteLLM, Portkey,
in-house routers) that Applied AI teams are asked to design and build.

Time is never read from a clock: every call that needs it takes an int `timestamp`.
Token count of a prompt = number of whitespace-separated words (`len(prompt.split())`).

### How the levels work
You build one codebase across **4 levels**. Open a level, read what it adds, extend your
existing code, run its tests. **Each level's tests include every earlier level's tests**, so a
change in level 3 must not break level 1 behaviour. Only the level 1 shells are in the
starter: you add the methods named in later level briefs yourself.

### Time guidance (~75 min total)
Level 1 ~15 min, level 2 ~15 min, level 3 ~20 min, level 4 ~25 min. If you blow past a
level's time, finish it simply and move on; interviewers score progress through levels.

### Interview tips
- Narrate: say what state you keep and why before you type.
- Keep level 1 dead simple (dicts and lists). Refactor only when a later level forces it.
- Read every rule in a level brief twice; most failures are a missed tie-break or error case.
- Run the tests after each method, not at the end.

levels.title: Level 1: models and budgets
levels.brief:
Build the core: models have a price, tenants have a credit budget, `route` charges it.

- `add_model(name: str, price_per_token: int) -> None` — `ValueError` if the name exists or the price is negative.
- `set_budget(tenant: str, credits: int) -> None` — sets (overwrites) the tenant's remaining credits; `ValueError` if negative.
- `remaining(tenant: str) -> int` — credits left (`KeyError` for an unknown tenant).
- `route(tenant, model, prompt, timestamp) -> dict`
  - `KeyError` for an unknown tenant or model; `ValueError` if the prompt has 0 tokens.
  - `cost = tokens * price_per_token`. If `cost <= remaining`, deduct it and return `{"status": "ok", "model": model, "cost": cost}`.
  - Otherwise charge nothing and return `{"status": "rejected", "model": None, "cost": 0}`.

```python
r = Router(); r.add_model("gpt-big", 3); r.set_budget("search", 20)
r.route("search", "gpt-big", "summarise this ticket please", 1)
# {'status': 'ok', 'model': 'gpt-big', 'cost': 12}
r.remaining("search")  # 8
```

tests.name: route charges the budget
tests.input: add_model(gpt-big, 3) → set_budget(search, 20) → route(search, gpt-big, "summarise this ticket please", 1)
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("gpt-big", 3)
r.set_budget("search", 20)
expect(r.route("search", "gpt-big", "summarise this ticket please", 1), {"status": "ok", "model": "gpt-big", "cost": 12})
expect(r.remaining("search"), 8)

tests.name: over budget is rejected, nothing charged
tests.input: budget 5, price 2, prompt of 3 words
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 2)
r.set_budget("t", 5)
expect(r.route("t", "m", "one two three", 1), {"status": "rejected", "model": None, "cost": 0})
expect(r.remaining("t"), 5)
expect(r.route("t", "m", "one two", 2)["cost"], 4)

tests.name: exact budget is allowed
tests.input: budget 6, price 2, 3-word prompt
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 2)
r.set_budget("t", 6)
expect(r.route("t", "m", "a b c", 1)["status"], "ok")
expect(r.remaining("t"), 0)

tests.name: unknown tenant / model / empty prompt
tests.input: route(ghost, m, ...), route(t, nope, ...), route(t, m, "   ")
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 10)
expect_raises(KeyError, r.route, "ghost", "m", "hi", 1)
expect_raises(KeyError, r.route, "t", "nope", "hi", 1)
expect_raises(ValueError, r.route, "t", "m", "   ", 1)
expect(r.remaining("t"), 10)

tests.name: validation on add_model / set_budget
tests.input: add_model(m,1) twice; add_model(x,-1); set_budget(t,-5)
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
expect_raises(ValueError, r.add_model, "m", 2)
expect_raises(ValueError, r.add_model, "x", -1)
expect_raises(ValueError, r.set_budget, "t", -5)
r.set_budget("t", 3)
r.set_budget("t", 9)
expect(r.remaining("t"), 9)

tests.name: tenants are isolated; free model costs 0
tests.input: two tenants, model price 0 and 5
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("free", 0)
r.add_model("pro", 5)
r.set_budget("a", 10)
r.set_budget("b", 10)
expect(r.route("a", "pro", "x y", 1)["cost"], 10)
expect(r.route("b", "free", "x y z w", 1), {"status": "ok", "model": "free", "cost": 0})
expect([r.remaining("a"), r.remaining("b")], [0, 10])

levels.title: Level 2: fallback
levels.brief:
Models go down and budgets run low. Add a fallback chain.

- `set_fallbacks(model: str, chain: list[str]) -> None` — ordered fallbacks for `model` (replaces any previous chain). `KeyError` if `model` or any chain entry is unknown; `ValueError` if `model` appears in its own chain.
- `mark_down(model: str, until: int) -> None` — the model is unavailable for requests with `timestamp < until` (`KeyError` if unknown).
- `route` now tries the requested model, then its chain in order (only the *requested* model's chain, no recursion). A candidate is skipped if it is down or its cost exceeds the remaining budget. The first usable one serves the request; `"model"` is the one actually used.
- If no candidate is usable: `"unavailable"` when **every** candidate was down, otherwise `"rejected"` (same dict shape, `model` None, `cost` 0).

```python
r.set_fallbacks("big", ["small"]); r.mark_down("big", until=100)
r.route("t", "big", "hello world", 50)   # {'status': 'ok', 'model': 'small', 'cost': ...}
```

tests.name: falls back when the model is down
tests.input: big(5), small(1); fallbacks big→[small]; mark_down(big, 100); route at t=50 then t=100
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("big", 5)
r.add_model("small", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 100)
r.set_fallbacks("big", ["small"])
r.mark_down("big", 100)
expect(r.route("t", "big", "hello world", 50), {"status": "ok", "model": "small", "cost": 2})
expect(r.route("t", "big", "hello world", 100), {"status": "ok", "model": "big", "cost": 10})

tests.name: falls back to a cheaper model when budget is low
tests.input: budget 4, big(5) small(1), 2-word prompt
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("big", 5)
r.add_model("small", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 4)
r.set_fallbacks("big", ["small"])
expect(r.route("t", "big", "hi there", 1), {"status": "ok", "model": "small", "cost": 2})
expect(r.remaining("t"), 2)

tests.name: all candidates down → unavailable
tests.input: big and small both down until 10; route at 5
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("big", 5)
r.add_model("small", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 100)
r.set_fallbacks("big", ["small"])
r.mark_down("big", 10)
r.mark_down("small", 10)
expect(r.route("t", "big", "hi", 5), {"status": "unavailable", "model": None, "cost": 0})
expect(r.remaining("t"), 100)

tests.name: one down, others unaffordable → rejected
tests.input: big down, small(3) costs more than budget 2
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("big", 5)
r.add_model("small", 3)
r.set_budget("t", 2)
r.set_fallbacks("big", ["small"])
r.mark_down("big", 10)
expect(r.route("t", "big", "hi", 5)["status"], "rejected")

tests.name: chain order is respected and not recursive
tests.input: a→[b, c], b→[d]; a and b down
tests.code:
r = Router()
for name in "abcd":
    r.add_model(name, 1)
r.set_budget("t", 100)
r.set_fallbacks("a", ["b", "c"])
r.set_fallbacks("b", ["d"])
r.mark_down("a", 10)
r.mark_down("b", 10)
expect(r.route("t", "a", "x", 1)["model"], "c")
r.mark_down("c", 10)
expect(r.route("t", "a", "x", 1)["status"], "unavailable")

tests.name: fallback validation
tests.input: set_fallbacks(a, [zzz]); set_fallbacks(a, [a]); mark_down(zzz, 5)
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("a", 1)
expect_raises(KeyError, r.set_fallbacks, "a", ["zzz"])
expect_raises(ValueError, r.set_fallbacks, "a", ["a"])
expect_raises(KeyError, r.mark_down, "zzz", 5)

levels.title: Level 3: response cache
levels.brief:
Identical prompts are common (retries, popular queries). Add an opt-in cache.

- `enable_cache(ttl: int) -> None` — turns caching on (`ValueError` if `ttl <= 0`). Before this is called nothing is cached, so earlier levels behave exactly as before.
- Cache key: `(requested model, prompt)`. It is **shared across tenants**.
- Only `"ok"` responses are stored, with the model that served them and the request's timestamp.
- A hit is valid while `timestamp < stored_at + ttl`. A hit returns `{"status": "cached", "model": <model that served the original>, "cost": 0}`, charges nothing and works even if that model is now down or the tenant's budget is 0. Hits do **not** refresh the TTL.
- Unknown tenant/model and empty prompt still raise as before (validate first).

```python
r.enable_cache(ttl=60)
r.route("a", "m", "what is rag", 0)    # ok, cost 3
r.route("b", "m", "what is rag", 59)   # {'status': 'cached', 'model': 'm', 'cost': 0}
r.route("b", "m", "what is rag", 60)   # expired → ok, charged
```

tests.name: cache hit is free and shared across tenants
tests.input: enable_cache(60); a routes "what is rag" at 0; b same at 59 and 60
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.set_budget("a", 10)
r.set_budget("b", 10)
r.enable_cache(60)
expect(r.route("a", "m", "what is rag", 0)["status"], "ok")
expect(r.route("b", "m", "what is rag", 59), {"status": "cached", "model": "m", "cost": 0})
expect(r.route("b", "m", "what is rag", 60), {"status": "ok", "model": "m", "cost": 3})
expect([r.remaining("a"), r.remaining("b")], [7, 7])

tests.name: no caching until enabled
tests.input: route the same prompt twice without enable_cache
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 10)
r.route("t", "m", "same", 0)
expect(r.route("t", "m", "same", 1)["status"], "ok")
expect(r.remaining("t"), 8)

tests.name: hit returns the fallback model and survives outage
tests.input: big down → served by small; then all down; repeat prompt
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("big", 5)
r.add_model("small", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 100)
r.set_fallbacks("big", ["small"])
r.enable_cache(100)
r.mark_down("big", 50)
expect(r.route("t", "big", "q", 1)["model"], "small")
r.mark_down("small", 50)
expect(r.route("t", "big", "q", 2), {"status": "cached", "model": "small", "cost": 0})
expect(r.route("t", "big", "other", 3)["status"], "unavailable")

tests.name: rejected responses are not cached; hit ignores empty budget
tests.input: budget 0 tenant; cached hit from another tenant
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.set_budget("poor", 0)
r.set_budget("rich", 5)
r.enable_cache(10)
expect(r.route("poor", "m", "hi", 0)["status"], "rejected")
expect(r.route("rich", "m", "hi", 1)["status"], "ok")
expect(r.route("poor", "m", "hi", 2)["status"], "cached")

tests.name: hits don't refresh ttl; key includes model
tests.input: ttl 10: store at 0, hit at 9, expired at 10; different model misses
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.add_model("n", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 100)
r.enable_cache(10)
r.route("t", "m", "hi", 0)
expect(r.route("t", "m", "hi", 9)["status"], "cached")
expect(r.route("t", "m", "hi", 10)["status"], "ok")
expect(r.route("t", "n", "hi", 11)["status"], "ok")

tests.name: validation still runs before the cache
tests.input: enable_cache(0); cached prompt for unknown tenant
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 5)
expect_raises(ValueError, r.enable_cache, 0)
r.enable_cache(5)
r.route("t", "m", "hi", 0)
expect_raises(KeyError, r.route, "ghost", "m", "hi", 1)

levels.title: Level 4: metrics
levels.brief:
Finance and on-call want numbers. Record every `route` call that returns a dict (calls that raise are not recorded).

- `metrics(start: int, end: int) -> dict` over requests with `start <= timestamp < end`:
  `{"requests", "ok", "cached", "rejected", "unavailable", "fallbacks", "spend", "by_model"}`
  - `fallbacks`: `"ok"` responses whose served model differs from the requested one.
  - `spend`: total credits charged; `by_model`: `{model: credits}` for `"ok"` responses only (models with no spend are absent).
- `top_tenants(n: int) -> list[tuple[str, int]]` — all-time spend, highest first, ties by tenant name ascending. Every tenant that has a budget appears (spend 0 if none). `n <= 0` → `[]`.

```python
r.metrics(0, 100)
# {'requests': 3, 'ok': 1, 'cached': 1, 'rejected': 1, 'unavailable': 0,
#  'fallbacks': 0, 'spend': 2, 'by_model': {'m': 2}}
```

tests.name: metrics count every outcome
tests.input: ok, cached, rejected in [0, 100)
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 2)
r.enable_cache(50)
r.route("t", "m", "a b", 1)
r.route("t", "m", "a b", 2)
r.route("t", "m", "c d", 3)
expect(r.metrics(0, 100), {"requests": 3, "ok": 1, "cached": 1, "rejected": 1, "unavailable": 0, "fallbacks": 0, "spend": 2, "by_model": {"m": 2}})

tests.name: window is half-open and fallbacks are counted
tests.input: big down; requests at 5, 10, 20; metrics(5, 20)
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("big", 3)
r.add_model("small", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 100)
r.set_fallbacks("big", ["small"])
r.mark_down("big", 15)
r.route("t", "big", "x", 5)
r.route("t", "big", "x", 10)
r.route("t", "big", "x", 20)
m = r.metrics(5, 20)
expect([m["requests"], m["fallbacks"], m["spend"], m["by_model"]], [2, 2, 2, {"small": 2}])
expect(r.metrics(20, 21)["by_model"], {"big": 3})

tests.name: empty window
tests.input: metrics(1000, 2000) with no requests there
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 5)
r.route("t", "m", "x", 1)
expect(r.metrics(1000, 2000), {"requests": 0, "ok": 0, "cached": 0, "rejected": 0, "unavailable": 0, "fallbacks": 0, "spend": 0, "by_model": {}})

tests.name: raising calls are not recorded; unavailable counted
tests.input: route with unknown tenant; all models down
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
r.set_budget("t", 5)
r.mark_down("m", 10)
expect_raises(KeyError, r.route, "ghost", "m", "x", 1)
r.route("t", "m", "x", 2)
m = r.metrics(0, 10)
expect([m["requests"], m["unavailable"]], [1, 1])

tests.name: top tenants by spend with name tie-break
tests.input: a spends 4, b 4, c 0, d 9; top_tenants(3), top_tenants(0)
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 1)
for t in "dcba":
    r.set_budget(t, 100)
r.route("b", "m", "w w w w", 1)
r.route("a", "m", "w w w w", 2)
r.route("d", "m", "w w w w w w w w w", 3)
expect(r.top_tenants(3), [("d", 9), ("a", 4), ("b", 4)])
expect(r.top_tenants(10)[-1], ("c", 0))
expect(r.top_tenants(0), [])

tests.name: cached hits add no spend
tests.input: two tenants share a cached prompt
tests.code:
r = Router()
r.add_model("m", 2)
r.set_budget("x", 10)
r.set_budget("y", 10)
r.enable_cache(100)
r.route("x", "m", "p q", 1)
r.route("y", "m", "p q", 2)
expect(r.top_tenants(2), [("x", 4), ("y", 0)])
expect(r.metrics(0, 10)["spend"], 4)

hints: Think of route as a pipeline of stages: validate, cache lookup, pick a model, charge, record. Each level adds one stage, so keep route small and push detail into helpers.

Keep dicts for prices, budgets, fallback chains and down-until timestamps. Build the candidate list as the requested model plus its chain, and track whether any candidate was up so you can tell unavailable from rejected. Wrap every return in one recording helper so metrics come for free.

Cache entries map (requested model, prompt) to (served model, stored timestamp); check it after validation but before routing, and only write it on ok. Metrics just filter the request log by a half-open window; top_tenants sorts by (-spend, name) over a spend dict seeded by set_budget. Everything is O(1) per request except metrics, which is O(log size).

ch-6.brief:
### Scenario
You own the **conversation memory** of a chat assistant. Every turn is stored, and before each
model call you must hand the model a context that fits its token window. Over four levels you
add a token-budgeted context window, rolling summaries, keyword search across history, and
retention/deletion rules for privacy. Memory management like this comes up in almost every
Applied AI system-design and practical round.

Token count of a text = number of whitespace-separated words (`len(text.split())`).
Timestamps are plain ints passed into methods. Message ids are global, start at 1, and are
never reused.

### How the levels work
You build one codebase across **4 levels**. Open a level, read what it adds, extend your
existing code, run its tests. **Each level's tests include every earlier level's tests**, so a
change in level 3 must not break level 1 behaviour. Only the level 1 shells are in the
starter: you add the methods named in later level briefs yourself.

### Time guidance (~75 min total)
Level 1 ~15 min, level 2 ~15 min, level 3 ~20 min, level 4 ~25 min. If you blow past a
level's time, finish it simply and move on; interviewers score progress through levels.

### Interview tips
- Narrate: say what state you keep and why before you type.
- Keep level 1 dead simple (dicts and lists). Refactor only when a later level forces it.
- Read every rule in a level brief twice; most failures are a missed tie-break or error case.
- Run the tests after each method, not at the end.

levels.title: Level 1: token-budgeted context
levels.brief:
- `ChatStore(max_tokens: int)` — `ValueError` if `max_tokens <= 0`.
- `add(conversation_id, role, text, timestamp) -> int` — `role` must be `"system"`, `"user"` or `"assistant"` (else `ValueError`). Returns the new message id (global counter from 1).
- `context(conversation_id) -> list[dict]` — the **newest contiguous** run of messages whose total tokens is `<= max_tokens`, oldest first, each as `{"role", "text"}`. Walk back from the newest message and stop at the first one that does not fit (do not skip it to grab older ones). Unknown conversation → `[]`.
- `token_count(conversation_id) -> int` — total tokens of all its messages (0 if unknown).

```python
s = ChatStore(max_tokens=5)
s.add("c1", "user", "hi there", 1)          # 1
s.add("c1", "assistant", "hello how can I help", 2)  # 2 (5 tokens)
s.context("c1")   # [{'role': 'assistant', 'text': 'hello how can I help'}]
s.token_count("c1")  # 7
```

tests.name: newest messages that fit
tests.input: max_tokens=5; add "hi there", "hello how can I help"
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(5)
expect(s.add("c1", "user", "hi there", 1), 1)
expect(s.add("c1", "assistant", "hello how can I help", 2), 2)
expect(s.context("c1"), [{"role": "assistant", "text": "hello how can I help"}])
expect(s.token_count("c1"), 7)

tests.name: everything fits, oldest first
tests.input: max_tokens=10; three short messages
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(10)
s.add("c", "system", "be brief", 1)
s.add("c", "user", "what is rag", 2)
s.add("c", "assistant", "retrieval augmented generation", 3)
expect([m["text"] for m in s.context("c")], ["be brief", "what is rag", "retrieval augmented generation"])

tests.name: stops at the first message that does not fit
tests.input: max_tokens=4; sizes 1, 5, 2, 1 tokens
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(4)
s.add("c", "user", "a", 1)
s.add("c", "user", "b b b b b", 2)
s.add("c", "user", "c c", 3)
s.add("c", "user", "d", 4)
expect(s.context("c"), [{"role": "user", "text": "c c"}, {"role": "user", "text": "d"}])

tests.name: ids are global across conversations
tests.input: add to c1, c2, c1
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
ids = [s.add("c1", "user", "x", 1), s.add("c2", "user", "y", 1), s.add("c1", "assistant", "z", 2)]
expect(ids, [1, 2, 3])
expect([m["text"] for m in s.context("c1")], ["x", "z"])
expect([m["text"] for m in s.context("c2")], ["y"])

tests.name: unknown conversation and bad input
tests.input: context(nope); add role=tool; ChatStore(0)
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(3)
expect(s.context("nope"), [])
expect(s.token_count("nope"), 0)
expect_raises(ValueError, s.add, "c", "tool", "x", 1)
expect_raises(ValueError, ChatStore, 0)

tests.name: newest alone too big → empty context
tests.input: max_tokens=2; newest message has 3 tokens
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(2)
s.add("c", "user", "ok", 1)
s.add("c", "user", "one two three", 2)
expect(s.context("c"), [])

levels.title: Level 2: rolling summaries
levels.brief:
Long chats fall out of the window. Let the app fold old turns into a summary.

- `summarize(conversation_id, upto_id: int, summary: str) -> int` — every **active** message of the conversation with id `<= upto_id` is folded away (removed from the context and from `token_count`) and the conversation's summary becomes `summary` (a newer summary replaces the old one; the app is expected to include the old summary's content). Returns the number of messages folded. `ValueError` if `upto_id` is not an active message of that conversation.
- `context` now always starts with `{"role": "summary", "text": summary}` when a summary exists, **even if it alone exceeds the budget**. Its tokens are spent first; the remaining budget is filled with the newest messages as in level 1.
- `token_count` = active message tokens + summary tokens.
- Folded messages are kept internally (level 3 searches them).

```python
s = ChatStore(7)
for i, t in enumerate(["a b", "c d", "e f", "g h"], 1): s.add("c", "user", t, i)
s.summarize("c", 2, "user said a to d")   # 2 messages folded
s.context("c")
# [{'role': 'summary', 'text': 'user said a to d'}, {'role': 'user', 'text': 'g h'}]
# (summary uses 5 of 7 tokens; "g h" fits, "e f" does not)
s.token_count("c")  # 9
```

tests.name: summary leads the context and uses budget first
tests.input: max_tokens=7; 4 two-word msgs; summarize(upto 2, "user said a to d")
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(7)
for i, t in enumerate(["a b", "c d", "e f", "g h"], 1):
    s.add("c", "user", t, i)
expect(s.summarize("c", 2, "user said a to d"), 2)
expect(s.context("c"), [{"role": "summary", "text": "user said a to d"}, {"role": "user", "text": "g h"}])
expect(s.token_count("c"), 9)

tests.name: second summary replaces the first
tests.input: summarize up to 1, then up to 3
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(50)
for i in range(1, 5):
    s.add("c", "user", f"m{i}", i)
s.summarize("c", 1, "first")
expect(s.summarize("c", 3, "first plus two three"), 2)
expect(s.context("c"), [{"role": "summary", "text": "first plus two three"}, {"role": "user", "text": "m4"}])

tests.name: oversized summary is still included
tests.input: max_tokens=2; summary of 4 tokens
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(2)
s.add("c", "user", "x", 1)
s.add("c", "user", "y", 2)
s.summarize("c", 1, "a long summary text")
expect(s.context("c"), [{"role": "summary", "text": "a long summary text"}])

tests.name: invalid upto_id
tests.input: upto_id from another conversation; already-folded id; unknown id
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(10)
a = s.add("c1", "user", "x", 1)
b = s.add("c2", "user", "y", 1)
expect_raises(ValueError, s.summarize, "c1", b, "s")
s.summarize("c1", a, "s")
expect_raises(ValueError, s.summarize, "c1", a, "again")
expect_raises(ValueError, s.summarize, "zzz", 99, "s")

tests.name: summarizing everything leaves only the summary
tests.input: summarize up to the newest id
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(10)
s.add("c", "user", "hello", 1)
last = s.add("c", "assistant", "hi", 2)
expect(s.summarize("c", last, "greetings exchanged"), 2)
expect(s.context("c"), [{"role": "summary", "text": "greetings exchanged"}])
expect(s.token_count("c"), 2)

levels.title: Level 3: search
levels.brief:
Users ask "what did I say about X?". Add keyword search over the whole history.

- `search(query: str, conversation_id: str | None = None, limit: int = 10) -> list[int]` — ids of messages containing **every** word of the query.
  - Words: lowercase runs of `[a-z0-9]` (so `"RAG,"` matches `"rag"`; `"rag"` does not match `"ragged"`).
  - Searches active **and folded** messages (summary texts are not searched). `None` means all conversations.
  - Newest (highest id) first, at most `limit` results; `limit <= 0` → `[]`.
  - `ValueError` if the query has no words (e.g. `""` or `"?!"`).

```python
s.search("vector db")          # [7, 3]
s.search("Vector", "c2")       # [5]
```

tests.name: all words must match, newest first
tests.input: msgs: "Use a vector DB", "vector search", "the DB is down, vector index fine"; search("vector db")
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
s.add("c1", "user", "Use a vector DB", 1)
s.add("c1", "assistant", "vector search", 2)
s.add("c2", "user", "the DB is down, vector index fine", 3)
expect(s.search("vector db"), [3, 1])
expect(s.search("VECTOR", "c1"), [2, 1])

tests.name: whole words, punctuation ignored
tests.input: "RAG, please" vs "ragged edge"; search("rag")
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
s.add("c", "user", "RAG, please", 1)
s.add("c", "user", "ragged edge", 2)
expect(s.search("rag"), [1])
expect(s.search("Rag!"), [1])

tests.name: folded messages are searchable, summaries are not
tests.input: fold msg 1 into summary "budget talk"; search budget, search pricing
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
s.add("c", "user", "pricing question", 1)
s.add("c", "user", "next", 2)
s.summarize("c", 1, "budget talk")
expect(s.search("pricing"), [1])
expect(s.search("budget"), [])

tests.name: limit and empty query
tests.input: 12 matching messages; limit default, limit=3, limit=0; query "?!"
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
for i in range(12):
    s.add("c", "user", f"note {i}", i)
expect(len(s.search("note")), 10)
expect(s.search("note", limit=3), [12, 11, 10])
expect(s.search("note", limit=0), [])
expect_raises(ValueError, s.search, "?!")

tests.name: scoped to one conversation; unknown conversation
tests.input: search("hi", "c2"); search("hi", "nope")
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
s.add("c1", "user", "hi", 1)
s.add("c2", "user", "hi", 2)
expect(s.search("hi", "c2"), [2])
expect(s.search("hi", "nope"), [])

levels.title: Level 4: retention and deletion
levels.brief:
Privacy review: data must not live forever, and users can delete chats.

- `expire(before: int) -> int` — permanently remove every message (active **or** folded, any conversation) with `timestamp < before`; return how many were removed. Summaries are kept. Removed messages disappear from `context`, `token_count` and `search`.
- `delete_conversation(conversation_id) -> bool` — remove its messages, folded messages and summary. `True` if the conversation existed, else `False`. Adding to the same id later starts a fresh conversation; message ids are **never reused**.

```python
s.expire(before=100)   # 2
s.delete_conversation("c1")  # True
s.delete_conversation("c1")  # False
```

tests.name: expire removes old messages everywhere
tests.input: msgs at t=10, 50, 150; expire(before=100)
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
s.add("c", "user", "old secret", 10)
s.add("c", "user", "older secret", 50)
s.add("c", "user", "new secret", 150)
expect(s.expire(100), 2)
expect(s.search("secret"), [3])
expect(s.context("c"), [{"role": "user", "text": "new secret"}])

tests.name: expire reaches folded messages but keeps the summary
tests.input: fold msg 1 (t=1); expire(5)
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
s.add("c", "user", "card number talk", 1)
s.add("c", "user", "later", 9)
s.summarize("c", 1, "payment discussed")
expect(s.expire(5), 1)
expect(s.search("card"), [])
expect(s.context("c")[0], {"role": "summary", "text": "payment discussed"})
expect(s.token_count("c"), 3)

tests.name: boundary: timestamp == before is kept
tests.input: msg at t=100; expire(100)
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(10)
s.add("c", "user", "edge", 100)
expect(s.expire(100), 0)
expect(s.token_count("c"), 1)

tests.name: delete conversation
tests.input: delete c1 (with summary) twice; c2 untouched
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
s.add("c1", "user", "alpha", 1)
s.add("c1", "user", "beta", 2)
s.summarize("c1", 1, "sum")
s.add("c2", "user", "alpha", 3)
expect(s.delete_conversation("c1"), True)
expect(s.delete_conversation("c1"), False)
expect([s.context("c1"), s.search("alpha")], [[], [3]])

tests.name: ids are never reused after deletion
tests.input: add 2, delete, add again
tests.code:
s = ChatStore(100)
s.add("c", "user", "x", 1)
s.add("c", "user", "y", 2)
s.delete_conversation("c")
expect(s.add("c", "user", "z", 3), 3)
expect(s.context("c"), [{"role": "user", "text": "z"}])
expect(s.delete_conversation("never"), False)

hints: Separate what the model sees (active messages plus a summary) from what you keep for search and compliance (folded messages). Most later-level bugs come from mixing those two lists.

Store per conversation: a list of active message dicts with id, role, text and timestamp, a list of folded messages, and an optional summary. Build the context by walking active messages from the newest, subtracting token costs from the budget left after the summary, and stopping at the first that does not fit.

summarize moves messages with id at most upto_id from active to folded after checking that upto_id is active. Search tokenises with a lowercase regex for alphanumeric runs and checks the query word set is a subset of each message's word set, over active and folded lists, then sorts ids descending and slices. expire filters both lists by timestamp; delete pops all three stores, and the global id counter is never reset.

ch-7.brief:
### Scenario
You are building the **leaderboard service** for an evaluation arena (think model or prompt
leaderboards, or a game). Scores arrive as events. Over four levels you add totals and
ranks, time-window boards ("this week"), competition ranking with ties and pagination, and
moderation (bans and account merges). The ordering rules are strict: most bugs here are
tie-break bugs, which is exactly what a practical round probes.

Timestamps are plain ints passed into methods. The global ordering everywhere is
**score descending, then player name ascending**.

### How the levels work
You build one codebase across **4 levels**. Open a level, read what it adds, extend your
existing code, run its tests. **Each level's tests include every earlier level's tests**, so a
change in level 3 must not break level 1 behaviour. Only the level 1 shells are in the
starter: you add the methods named in later level briefs yourself.

### Time guidance (~75 min total)
Level 1 ~15 min, level 2 ~15 min, level 3 ~20 min, level 4 ~25 min. If you blow past a
level's time, finish it simply and move on; interviewers score progress through levels.

### Interview tips
- Narrate: say what state you keep and why before you type.
- Keep level 1 dead simple (dicts and lists). Refactor only when a later level forces it.
- Read every rule in a level brief twice; most failures are a missed tie-break or error case.
- Run the tests after each method, not at the end.

levels.title: Level 1: totals and ranks
levels.brief:
- `add_score(player, points, timestamp) -> int` — adds to the player's total and returns the new total. `points` must be a positive `int` (not bool), else `ValueError`.
- `score(player) -> int` — total, `0` for unknown players.
- `top(n) -> list[tuple[str, int]]` — first `n` `(player, total)` pairs by score desc, name asc. `n <= 0` → `[]`.
- `rank(player) -> int | None` — 1-based position in that ordering (ties get distinct positions by name). `None` if unknown.

```python
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("ann", 10, 1); lb.add_score("bob", 30, 2); lb.add_score("ann", 25, 3)
lb.top(2)      # [('ann', 35), ('bob', 30)]
lb.rank("bob") # 2
```

tests.name: totals, top and rank
tests.input: ann+10, bob+30, ann+25; top(2), rank(bob)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
expect(lb.add_score("ann", 10, 1), 10)
lb.add_score("bob", 30, 2)
expect(lb.add_score("ann", 25, 3), 35)
expect(lb.top(2), [("ann", 35), ("bob", 30)])
expect(lb.rank("bob"), 2)

tests.name: ties broken by name
tests.input: cat 5, abe 5, bea 7; top(3)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("cat", 5, 1)
lb.add_score("abe", 5, 2)
lb.add_score("bea", 7, 3)
expect(lb.top(3), [("bea", 7), ("abe", 5), ("cat", 5)])
expect([lb.rank("abe"), lb.rank("cat")], [2, 3])

tests.name: unknown player and n bounds
tests.input: score(zed), rank(zed), top(0), top(10) with 1 player
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 1, 1)
expect([lb.score("zed"), lb.rank("zed")], [0, None])
expect(lb.top(0), [])
expect(lb.top(10), [("a", 1)])

tests.name: invalid points
tests.input: add_score(a, 0), add_score(a, -3), add_score(a, 1.5), add_score(a, True)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
for bad in (0, -3, 1.5, True):
    expect_raises(ValueError, lb.add_score, "a", bad, 1, label=repr(bad))
expect(lb.score("a"), 0)

tests.name: empty board
tests.input: top(3) and rank on a new board
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
expect(lb.top(3), [])
expect(lb.rank("x"), None)

levels.title: Level 2: time windows
levels.brief:
Product wants "this week's" board without losing the all-time board.

- `score_in_window(player, start, end) -> int` — points from events with `start <= timestamp < end` (0 if none).
- `top_in_window(n, start, end) -> list[tuple[str, int]]` — like `top`, but using window totals; players with no points in the window are absent. `ValueError` if `start >= end`.
- All-time methods are unchanged.

```python
lb.add_score("ann", 10, 1); lb.add_score("bob", 5, 8); lb.add_score("ann", 1, 9)
lb.top_in_window(5, 5, 10)   # [('bob', 5), ('ann', 1)]
```

tests.name: window board vs all-time board
tests.input: ann 10@1, bob 5@8, ann 1@9; top_in_window(5, 5, 10)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("ann", 10, 1)
lb.add_score("bob", 5, 8)
lb.add_score("ann", 1, 9)
expect(lb.top_in_window(5, 5, 10), [("bob", 5), ("ann", 1)])
expect(lb.top(5), [("ann", 11), ("bob", 5)])

tests.name: half-open boundaries
tests.input: events at 10 and 20; window [10, 20)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 3, 10)
lb.add_score("a", 4, 20)
expect(lb.score_in_window("a", 10, 20), 3)
expect(lb.score_in_window("a", 20, 21), 4)
expect(lb.score_in_window("b", 0, 100), 0)

tests.name: ties inside a window
tests.input: x 2, y 2, z 1 in window; top_in_window(2, 0, 10)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("y", 2, 1)
lb.add_score("x", 2, 2)
lb.add_score("z", 1, 3)
lb.add_score("z", 50, 99)
expect(lb.top_in_window(2, 0, 10), [("x", 2), ("y", 2)])

tests.name: empty and invalid windows
tests.input: top_in_window(3, 100, 200); start == end
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 1, 1)
expect(lb.top_in_window(3, 100, 200), [])
expect_raises(ValueError, lb.top_in_window, 3, 5, 5)

tests.name: events out of time order
tests.input: add at t=50 then t=5; window [0, 10)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 7, 50)
lb.add_score("a", 2, 5)
expect(lb.top_in_window(1, 0, 10), [("a", 2)])

levels.title: Level 3: ties and pagination
levels.brief:
The UI shows *competition ranking* ("1, 1, 3"): tied scores share the place of the first of them.

- `rank_info(player) -> dict | None` — `{"rank": competition rank, "score": total, "tied_with": [other players with the same score, name asc]}`; `None` if unknown.
- `page(page: int, size: int) -> dict` — `{"items": [(rank, player, score), ...], "total_players": int, "total_pages": int}` over the all-time ordering (score desc, name asc) with competition ranks. Pages are 1-based; a page past the end has `items == []`. `ValueError` if `page < 1` or `size < 1`.
- `rank()` from level 1 keeps its old meaning (distinct positions).

```python
# scores: ann 9, bob 9, cy 5
lb.rank_info("bob")  # {'rank': 1, 'score': 9, 'tied_with': ['ann']}
lb.page(2, 2)        # {'items': [(3, 'cy', 5)], 'total_players': 3, 'total_pages': 2}
```

tests.name: competition rank and pages
tests.input: ann 9, bob 9, cy 5; rank_info(bob), page(2, 2)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("bob", 9, 1)
lb.add_score("ann", 9, 2)
lb.add_score("cy", 5, 3)
expect(lb.rank_info("bob"), {"rank": 1, "score": 9, "tied_with": ["ann"]})
expect(lb.page(2, 2), {"items": [(3, "cy", 5)], "total_players": 3, "total_pages": 2})
expect(lb.rank("bob"), 2)

tests.name: 1, 2, 2, 4 ranking
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
for name, pts in [("d", 3), ("c", 7), ("b", 7), ("a", 10)]:
    lb.add_score(name, pts, 1)
expect(lb.page(1, 10)["items"], [(1, "a", 10), (2, "b", 7), (2, "c", 7), (4, "d", 3)])
expect(lb.rank_info("d"), {"rank": 4, "score": 3, "tied_with": []})

tests.name: tie spanning a page boundary
tests.input: four players all 5; page(2, 3)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
for name in ["w", "x", "y", "z"]:
    lb.add_score(name, 5, 1)
expect(lb.page(2, 3)["items"], [(1, "z", 5)])
expect(lb.rank_info("w")["tied_with"], ["x", "y", "z"])

tests.name: page past the end and empty board
tests.input: page(5, 2) with 3 players; page(1, 5) on empty
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
expect(lb.page(1, 5), {"items": [], "total_players": 0, "total_pages": 0})
for name in "abc":
    lb.add_score(name, 1, 1)
expect(lb.page(5, 2), {"items": [], "total_players": 3, "total_pages": 2})

tests.name: invalid page arguments and unknown player
tests.input: page(0, 2), page(1, 0), rank_info(ghost)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 1, 1)
expect_raises(ValueError, lb.page, 0, 2)
expect_raises(ValueError, lb.page, 1, 0)
expect(lb.rank_info("ghost"), None)

levels.title: Level 4: moderation
levels.brief:
Cheaters and duplicate accounts appear. Add moderation without corrupting the boards.

- `ban(player) -> bool` — hides the player from `top`, `rank`, `top_in_window`, `rank_info`, `page` (ranks of everyone else close up). `rank`/`rank_info` return `None` for a banned player. `add_score` for a banned player raises `PermissionError`. `score`/`score_in_window` still report raw numbers (moderators need them). Returns `False` if the player is unknown or already banned.
- `unban(player) -> bool` — restores them; `False` if not banned.
- `merge_players(source, target) -> int` — moves all of `source`'s events (keeping their timestamps) to `target`, so windows stay correct; `source` disappears. Returns `target`'s new total. `ValueError` if `source == target`, `KeyError` if `source` unknown, `PermissionError` if either is banned. `target` may be new.

```python
lb.ban("cheat")         # True
lb.merge_players("ann_alt", "ann")  # ann's new total
```

tests.name: ban hides a player and ranks close up
tests.input: a 50, b 40, c 30; ban(a); top(3), rank(b), page(1, 5)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 50, 1)
lb.add_score("b", 40, 1)
lb.add_score("c", 30, 1)
expect(lb.ban("a"), True)
expect(lb.top(3), [("b", 40), ("c", 30)])
expect([lb.rank("b"), lb.rank("a"), lb.rank_info("a")], [1, None, None])
expect(lb.page(1, 5)["items"], [(1, "b", 40), (2, "c", 30)])

tests.name: banned player cannot score; raw score still visible
tests.input: ban(a); add_score(a, 5); score(a); unban(a)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 10, 1)
lb.ban("a")
expect_raises(PermissionError, lb.add_score, "a", 5, 2)
expect(lb.score("a"), 10)
expect(lb.unban("a"), True)
expect(lb.top(1), [("a", 10)])

tests.name: ban/unban return values
tests.input: ban(ghost), ban twice, unban not-banned
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 1, 1)
expect(lb.ban("ghost"), False)
expect([lb.ban("a"), lb.ban("a")], [True, False])
expect([lb.unban("a"), lb.unban("a")], [True, False])

tests.name: banned players vanish from window boards too
tests.input: a and b score in window; ban(b)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 1, 5)
lb.add_score("b", 9, 5)
lb.ban("b")
expect(lb.top_in_window(5, 0, 10), [("a", 1)])
expect(lb.score_in_window("b", 0, 10), 9)

tests.name: merge keeps event timestamps
tests.input: ann 10@1, alt 5@20, alt 3@2; merge(alt → ann)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("ann", 10, 1)
lb.add_score("alt", 5, 20)
lb.add_score("alt", 3, 2)
expect(lb.merge_players("alt", "ann"), 18)
expect([lb.score("alt"), lb.rank("alt")], [0, None])
expect(lb.score_in_window("ann", 0, 10), 13)
expect(lb.top(5), [("ann", 18)])

tests.name: merge errors and merge into a new name
tests.input: merge(a, a), merge(ghost, a), merge with banned; merge(a → fresh)
tests.code:
lb = Leaderboard()
lb.add_score("a", 4, 1)
lb.add_score("b", 2, 1)
expect_raises(ValueError, lb.merge_players, "a", "a")
expect_raises(KeyError, lb.merge_players, "ghost", "a")
lb.ban("b")
expect_raises(PermissionError, lb.merge_players, "a", "b")
expect(lb.merge_players("a", "fresh"), 4)
expect(lb.rank_info("fresh"), {"rank": 1, "score": 4, "tied_with": []})

hints: Store raw score events, not just totals: windows and merges both need to know when each point arrived. Write the ordering (score descending, name ascending) once and reuse it everywhere.

Keep a totals dict for fast all-time reads and an event list of (timestamp, player, points). One helper sorts any totals dict by the shared key and filters out banned players; window boards just build a totals dict from filtered events and call the same helper.

Competition rank: walk the sorted list and when the score changes set the place to the current 1-based index, otherwise keep the previous place. Pagination slices that ranked list at (page - 1) * size, and total pages is ceiling division. A merge rewrites the player name in the event list and moves the total, so windows stay correct; sorting is O(P log P) per query, which is fine here; mention a sorted structure or a heap if asked about scale.

ch-8.brief:
### Scenario
Your company ships AI features (a new model, a new prompt, a new retrieval pipeline) behind
**feature flags** so they can be targeted, rolled out gradually and switched off fast. Over
four levels you build flags with targeting rules, deterministic percentage rollouts, an
audit log with rollback, and prerequisite flags with cycle detection. This mirrors how
Applied AI teams run online experiments and safe launches.

A *user* is a plain dict such as `{"id": "u1", "country": "IN", "plan": "pro"}`.

### How the levels work
You build one codebase across **4 levels**. Open a level, read what it adds, extend your
existing code, run its tests. **Each level's tests include every earlier level's tests**, so a
change in level 3 must not break level 1 behaviour. Only the level 1 shells are in the
starter: you add the methods named in later level briefs yourself.

### Time guidance (~75 min total)
Level 1 ~15 min, level 2 ~15 min, level 3 ~20 min, level 4 ~25 min. If you blow past a
level's time, finish it simply and move on; interviewers score progress through levels.

### Interview tips
- Narrate: say what state you keep and why before you type.
- Keep level 1 dead simple (dicts and lists). Refactor only when a later level forces it.
- Read every rule in a level brief twice; most failures are a missed tie-break or error case.
- Run the tests after each method, not at the end.

levels.title: Level 1: flags and targeting rules
levels.brief:
- `create_flag(name, default: bool) -> None` — `ValueError` if it exists.
- `set_default(name, value: bool) -> None` — `KeyError` for unknown flags (same for every method below that takes a flag name).
- `add_rule(name, attribute, values: list, result: bool) -> None` — appends a rule; `ValueError` if `values` is empty.
- `evaluate(name, user: dict) -> bool` — rules are checked **in the order added**; the first rule where `attribute` is in `user` and `user[attribute] in values` decides (returns its `result`). If none match, return the flag's default.

```python
f = FlagService()
f.create_flag("new-checkout", False)
f.add_rule("new-checkout", "country", ["IN", "SG"], True)
f.evaluate("new-checkout", {"id": "u1", "country": "IN"})  # True
f.evaluate("new-checkout", {"id": "u2", "country": "US"})  # False
```

tests.name: rule match vs default
tests.input: new-checkout default False; rule country in [IN, SG] → True; users IN and US
tests.code:
f = FlagService()
f.create_flag("new-checkout", False)
f.add_rule("new-checkout", "country", ["IN", "SG"], True)
expect(f.evaluate("new-checkout", {"id": "u1", "country": "IN"}), True)
expect(f.evaluate("new-checkout", {"id": "u2", "country": "US"}), False)

tests.name: first matching rule wins
tests.input: rule plan in [free] → False, then country in [IN] → True; IN free user
tests.code:
f = FlagService()
f.create_flag("x", True)
f.add_rule("x", "plan", ["free"], False)
f.add_rule("x", "country", ["IN"], True)
expect(f.evaluate("x", {"plan": "free", "country": "IN"}), False)
expect(f.evaluate("x", {"plan": "pro", "country": "IN"}), True)

tests.name: missing attribute does not match
tests.input: rule on beta; user without beta key
tests.code:
f = FlagService()
f.create_flag("x", False)
f.add_rule("x", "beta", [True], True)
expect(f.evaluate("x", {"id": "u"}), False)

tests.name: set_default changes the fallback

levels.title: Level 2: percentage rollouts
levels.brief:
Roll a feature out to a stable slice of users.

- `bucket(name, user_id) -> int` (static or instance method) — exactly `zlib.crc32(f"{name}:{user_id}".encode("utf-8")) % 100`. Deterministic: the same user always lands in the same bucket for a flag.
- `set_rollout(name, percent: int | None) -> None` — `0..100` inclusive (else `ValueError`); `None` removes the rollout.
- `evaluate`: rules still win first. If no rule matched and a rollout is set, return `bucket(name, user["id"]) < percent` (this **replaces** the default). `ValueError` if the user has no `"id"` in that case. With no rollout, behaviour is unchanged.

Known buckets for flag `"new-checkout"`: u1 → 18, u2 → 0, u3 → 94, bob → 12, carol → 59.

```python
f.set_rollout("new-checkout", 20)
f.evaluate("new-checkout", {"id": "u1"})   # True  (18 < 20)
f.evaluate("new-checkout", {"id": "u3"})   # False (94)
```

levels.title: Level 3: audit log and rollback
levels.brief:
Every change must be traceable and reversible. This level makes you **retrofit** logging into the methods you already wrote.

- Every successful mutation appends an audit entry. A global sequence number starts at 1 and increases across **all** flags. Actions: `"create"`, `"set_default"`, `"add_rule"`, `"set_rollout"` (and `"rollback"` below). Failed calls (those that raise) log nothing.
- `audit_log(name) -> list[dict]` — that flag's entries, oldest first, each `{"seq": int, "action": str}`.
- `rollback(name, seq) -> None` — restore the flag's full configuration (default, rules, rollout) to what it was right **after** entry `seq`, then log a `"rollback"` entry. `ValueError` if `seq` is not an entry of that flag.

```python
f.create_flag("a", False)        # seq 1
f.create_flag("b", True)         # seq 2
f.add_rule("a", "plan", ["pro"], True)  # seq 3
f.audit_log("a")  # [{'seq': 1, 'action': 'create'}, {'seq': 3, 'action': 'add_rule'}]
f.rollback("a", 1)   # rules gone again; logs seq 4 'rollback'
```

levels.title: Level 4: prerequisites
levels.brief:
A feature may only turn on when another feature is on (e.g. `"agent-mode"` requires `"new-model"`).

- `add_prerequisite(name, other, required: bool) -> None` — `name` can only be on for a user when `evaluate(other, user) == required`. Logged as `"add_prerequisite"`; part of the flag's config, so `rollback` restores prerequisites too. `KeyError` if either flag is unknown. `ValueError` (and nothing logged) if it would create a cycle, including `name == other`.
- `evaluate`: check prerequisites first, in the order added; if any is unmet return `False` immediately (rules, rollout and default are not consulted).
- `rollback` must also raise `ValueError` (and change nothing) if the restored prerequisites would now form a cycle.
- `evaluate_all(user) -> dict[str, bool]` — every flag's value, keys in sorted order.

```python
f.add_prerequisite("agent-mode", "new-model", True)
f.evaluate("agent-mode", user)  # False unless new-model is on for user
```

hints: Model each flag as one plain config dict (default, rules, rollout, prerequisites). Evaluation is an ordered decision list, and both the audit log and rollback become easy if the whole config can be copied as one value.

evaluate checks prerequisites, then rules in order, then the rollout bucket, then the default. For the audit log, add one helper that bumps a global sequence number and stores the action together with a deep copy of the flag config, and call it at the end of every successful mutation.

Rollback finds the entry by seq and flag name, deep-copies its stored config back and logs a rollback entry; deep copies matter because rules are lists that later edits mutate. Cycle detection is a DFS from the new prerequisite following prerequisite edges, failing if it reaches the flag being edited; run the same check for every prerequisite a rollback would restore. Evaluation is O(rules + prerequisite depth) per call.
